title: Never share your OTP or PIN
rule: No real bank, company or officer ever needs your OTP, PIN or CVV.
summary: An OTP is the key to your money. Anyone who asks for it is a thief.
doThis: Keep the OTP on your phone. Type it only in the bank's own app.
If a caller asks for a code, cut the call.
If you shared an OTP, call your bank at once and block the account.
redFlags: "Read out the code we just sent you"
"We are from the bank security team"
"Your account will be blocked in 10 minutes"

title: Scanning a QR always SENDS money
rule: You never scan a QR or approve a request to RECEIVE money.
summary: Scanning a QR or approving a UPI request takes money OUT of your account — never in.
doThis: Read the name and amount on the confirm screen before you enter the PIN.
Decline any "collect request" you did not start.
Get a shop's UPI ID from their own board or app, not from a stranger.
redFlags: "Scan this to get your refund / cashback / prize"
A big amount already filled in that you did not type
A QR sticker pasted on top of another one
Name says a shop, but the UPI ID looks personal

title: Do not tap links in surprise messages
rule: Open a bank or government site by typing its name yourself — never from a link.
summary: Scam messages copy a real company and push you to tap a link and log in.
doThis: If a message says there is a problem, open the official app directly.
Check the sender — a bank never texts from a normal 10-digit number.
When unsure, call the number printed on your card or passbook.
redFlags: "Your KYC / PAN / account needs updating — click here"
The web address is odd: paypa1.com, sbi-verify.tk

title: Check the website address letter by letter
rule: A fake site looks the same but the address is slightly wrong.
summary: Scam sites copy a brand's look but live on a slightly different address.
doThis: Read the domain slowly: paypal.com — not paypa1.com or paypal-secure.xyz.
Look for https and the real company name in the address.
Type the address yourself for anything to do with money.
redFlags: The page asks for your password the moment it opens

title: Police never arrest you over a video call
rule: No real officer video-calls to threaten arrest and demand money.
summary: "Digital arrest" scammers wear a uniform on a call, say a parcel or case is in your name, and keep you on the line until you pay.
doThis: Cut the call. A real notice comes on paper, in person.
Do not stay on the line, do not pay, do not move money to a "safe account".
Tell a family member, then report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.
redFlags: "Your Aadhaar / parcel is linked to a crime"
"Stay on the call, do not tell anyone"
"Transfer the money for verification, you will get it back"

title: You did not win. There is no easy job.
rule: If you must pay a fee to get money or a job, it is a scam.
summary: Lottery, lucky-draw, work-from-home and "rate this video" offers ask a small fee first — which you never get back.
doThis: Ignore "you have won" messages for lotteries you never entered.
Never pay a registration / processing / deposit fee for a job.
Block and delete. Do not forward to friends.
redFlags: "Earn ₹5000 a day from home, pay ₹500 to start"
A Telegram group that pays you to like or rate things
